newsitem.title: UK: Northern Foods dairy business recovers.
newsitem.headline: Northern Foods dairy business recovers.

text.p: LONDON, June 10 (Reuter) British dairy and food company Northern Foods is benefiting from a fall in its raw milk prices, enabling its dairy division to stage a recovery, chairman Christopher Haskins said on Tuesday.

His comments were attached to the group's annual accounts which showed a 7.1 percent increase in pre-tax profits to 128.3 million pounds and a strong 20 percent increase in its prepared foods business profit to 98.6 million.
"The dairy business is enjoying a substantial profit recovery as the raw milk price falls," said Haskins.
But Nothern's dairy division posted trading profits of 44.8 million for the year, 26 percent lower than in 1995/96, due to the 17 million pound ($27.8 million) impact of lower commodity prices.
Total group sales were 3.3 percent lower in the year at 1.883 billion with continued growth in prepared foods more than offset by the effects of changes and lower commodity prices on the dairy side.
Meat products turnover was 4.7 percent down at 227.3 million after an estimated 12 million pound hit from the scare over the spread of mad cow disease to humans.
Dairy sales were down 12 percent at 789 million pounds with the sale of some of the group's doorstep delivery businesses accounting for about 34 percent of the reduction.
